title: Identity coefficient normalization of compact-support restriction
statement: Let $X,Y$ be schemes and $c=(j,p)$ a compactification of $f:X\to Y$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. Let $A$ be any finite commutative ring. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] use the entire unbounded derived categories of intrinsic constant-$A$-module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $F=Rp_*j_!$ for the fixed-compactification functor [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], $\sigma_1:F\operatorname{Res}_{1_A}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{1_A}F$ for its specified coefficient restriction comparison [lem-sf-compact-support-restriction-of-scalars], and $i_T:\operatorname{Res}_{1_A}\cong\mathrm{id}$ for the canonical identity restriction comparison [def-coef-scalar-restriction-identity]. For every $H\in D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ and any ring map $q:A\to A$ equipped with an equality $h:q=1_A$, $\sigma_{q,H};(\mathrm{eqToIso}(\operatorname{Res}_Y(h));i_Y)_{FH}=F((\mathrm{eqToIso}(\operatorname{Res}_X(h));i_X)_H)$. This only concerns the identity coefficient map and imposes no geometric boundedness or coefficient invertibility requirement.

proof.text: Substitute the supplied equality q = RingHom.id A. Proof irrelevance and the identity eqToIso reduce compactSupportCoefficientResId to sfOpenDerivedCoefficientRestrictionId. Its component on Q(J) is the scalar localization factor followed by Q of the degreewise ordinary identity comparison: use the canonical derived identity factor and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso_fac.

For direct image g and identity coefficients, let F be ordinary canonical direct image, x and y the two ordinary restrictions, and c the identity-on-sections ordinary comparison. The ordinary identity comparisons give y-to-identity and x-to-identity maps of squares: evaluate on sections and use their sectionwise identity normalizations. The identity square for F and its right-derived functor is unit-normalized by the identity laws. Apply normalized_naturality to this square and compactSupportScalarDirectNormalization. The preceding localization-factor equation verifies the two comparison hypotheses. Taking a component and cancelling the inverse of sfDerivedImageRestriction proves its identity law at every unbounded derived object.

Use the already proved sfOpenRestriction_derived_id for the open immersion c.i, on the given unbounded input. This supplies exactly the open identity square with the same canonical scalar identity comparisons.

Expand compactSupportCoefficientComparison and sfCompactSupportRestriction into direct image of the open comparison followed by the proper comparison. Apply the direct-image identity law at the open extension of K. Combine the resulting two direct-image maps with map_comp and apply the open identity law. The result is the composite compact-support functor applied to the input identity comparison, as required.

theorem compactSupportRestriction_identity
    {X Y : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ Y} (c : Compactification f)
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [Finite A]
    (q : A →+* A) (hq : q = RingHom.id A) (K : proEtaleDerivedCategory X A) :
    (compactSupportCoefficientComparison c q).hom.app K ≫
        (compactSupportCoefficientResId Y A q hq).hom.app
          ((sfAmbientCompactSupportCandidate A c).obj K) =
      (sfAmbientCompactSupportCandidate A c).map
        ((compactSupportCoefficientResId X A q hq).hom.app K)
